title: the weapons
hook: six nights awake, a silent sage, and an arrow that chooses not to kill

segments.voice: Yesterday: the weapons, part two. Rama asked how to call them back, and the sage taught him the withdrawal. Did you think about how to call something back before you started it? Today the week closes. Day five hundred four.

At Siddhashrama, Vishvamitra begins his sacrifice and takes a vow of silence. From now on, he can't say a word. So the hermits tell the boys: for six days and six nights, you have to guard him. Rama and Lakshmana stand watch, bows ready, and don't sleep. Five days pass. Nothing. On the sixth, the altar fire suddenly flares up on its own. The sky goes dark. And out of the dark comes a roar, and a rain of blood.
screen: `A VOW OF SILENCE.` → `SIX NIGHTS ON WATCH.` → `THE SIXTH DAY: A RAIN OF BLOOD.`

segments.voice: Maricha and Subahu have come, with their followers, to wreck the rite. Rama sees them and says to Lakshmana: watch this. He picks up the manava weapon, the one named for Manu, the first human, and fires it at Maricha's chest. It doesn't kill him. It lifts him and hurls him a hundred yojanas, far out over the sea, where he falls, stunned, but alive. And Rama says it plainly: the manava has knocked him senseless, but it hasn't taken his life. Then the fire weapon for Subahu, who falls dead. Then the wind weapon scatters the rest. The sacrifice is finished. Vishvamitra, his vow complete, turns to Rama and says: you've made the name of this place come true. Siddhashrama, the hermitage of accomplishment. Hold onto Maricha. He's still out there, alive, and he will come back in this story wearing a very different shape. Now the week, from the top. A father's plea that his son isn't yet sixteen. Vasishtha's counsel and the sage's dawn verse. A forest that used to be farmland. Rama asking first, and disarming before destroying. The weapons appearing with joined palms. The question of how to call them back. And today, the first real use: one enemy spared, and a promise kept.
screen: `THE MANAVA FOR MARICHA.` · `HURLED OVER THE SEA, STILL ALIVE.` · `THE FIRE WEAPON FOR SUBAHU.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `SIDDHASHRAMA: ACCOMPLISHED.`

segments.voice: Sit as if you're on watch. Not tense. Just awake. Let your eyes rest low, your back long, your breath even. Notice the sounds around you, each one arriving and passing, the way the boys watched the dark for six nights. If your attention wanders, come back to the watch without scolding yourself. Steady, alert, and calm. The bell holds the time.
The weapons. At Siddhashrama, Rama uses them for the first time: the manava hurls Maricha out to sea alive, and the sacrifice is completed.
Your line: the weapons. Today, when you win a small conflict, leave the other person a way to walk off whole. Day five hundred four.

screen: `DAY 504 COUNTS.` → `A WEEK ON THE ROAD WITH THE SAGE, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: AHALYA RESTORED.`

howItsDone: Ramayana tellings mark Maricha's survival here because he returns in the Aranya Kanda as the golden deer; teachers often point out that Rama chose a weapon that would stun, not kill.

myth: the manava hurls him far over the sea, stunned but alive.
Vishvamitra keeps silent during the sacrifice
he's under a vow, so the boys stand guard for six days and nights.
Siddhashrama means something like the hermitage of accomplishment
and Vishvamitra says Rama has made the name come true.

fork.setup: you're Rama. Maricha attacks the sacrifice. you hold the manava weapon. what do you do?
options: strike him so he's hurled far away, alive.
fork.reveal: the manava hurls Maricha a hundred yojanas over the sea, senseless but alive. he'll be back, as the golden deer.

trapdoor: what you thought: the first battle is all about killing demons.
what it means: Rama chooses which weapon for whom, and spares Maricha.
what a scholar hears: Bala Kanda 30 has the manava, agneya and vayavya; Maricha's survival sets up his return as the golden deer in the Aranya Kanda.
